Kuchyna Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kuchyňa, Slovakia

Not demolished. Kuchyňa, first mentioned in 1206 as Cuhnamezej, was home to Slovaks, Germans, and Jews, though the exact date of Jewish settlement is unknown; before WWII several Jewish families made their living in agriculture and trade, running a general store and butchery among other businesses. Relations with the mostly Catholic population were good, worsening only after the Slovak State's establishment brought hostility from some members of the Hlinka Guard. This cemetery, of unknown establishment date, sits beside a plague (cholera) cemetery established in 1831. According to the 1942 census, 23 Jews lived in the village; most were deported to concentration camps during WWII, with some fighting in the Slovak National Uprising. The few who returned after the war soon left, mostly for Israel.
